questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go to California because I love it there. I chose UCSD because of the classes and the beautiful campus and also the location and weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult to get to know the ucsd different sites and systems

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: ISPO did some welcoming camps and made themselves available to assist us with questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It worked out really well for me - I feel very lucky. I used facebook groups to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a good opportunity to meet other young people that may be from the area and to get to know more of the city and culture thats not just campus life

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Find the classes you want, see if they are active for the quarter, when the registration opens you can choose up to 12 units and there after you can choose more and drop classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was quite confusing for me and ended up writing both student counseling and the professors and ended up with the right amount of classes

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I needed and had some classes because I had to have 12 units

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research before the registration opens, be ready when it does, ask for help, write the professors sooner rather than later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the classes were appropriate, not too difficult but very interesting and very capable professors!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Even thought some lectures are with a lot of people, you feel closer to the program, course material and professor. There's a lot more tests, quizzes and assignments than at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. quarter: social psychology, popular culture, sexuality and sexual identities
2. quarter: psychology of human sexuality, qualitative interviewing, philosophy and feminism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: social psychology, sexuality and sexual identities, psychology of human sexuality

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: A lot of beautiful hikes, beaches, wine country, nice areas in and around SD, go to a baseball game, surf camp

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Lived with two american guys which definitly made it easier, spend a lot of time with them and their friends

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No...

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are really kind and interested, a lot of amazing food and diversity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Its very expensive, so make sure you have the money (but so worth it!)
2. Highly recommend living off campus (near the beaches)
3. Explore and experience, you will pass your classes so make sure to also do something else than school

questions.answer: The social life, friends I got here!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money, very expensive to live in SD
